You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Fdd2 (space-group number 43, Hall symbol F 2 -2d). The supplied input cell is not the conventional F-centered cell: it is a 16-atom primitive-like setting with lattice parameters a = 7.79098956 Å, b = 6.65356087 Å, c = 6.60119496 Å, α = 71.99919188°, β = 54.31196333°, and γ = 53.68884479°. The declared input composition is Rb₂P₂H₄O₈, corresponding to 16 atoms in this input cell. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where P has rows (−1/2, 1.018179684602515×10⁻¹⁶, −1/2), (0.49999999999999994, 1/2, −6.082375016461746×10⁻¹⁸), and (5.930306560194863×10⁻¹⁷, −0.5000000000000001, −0.49999999999999994), and the origin shift s is (0, −5.551115123125783×10⁻¹⁷, −5.551115123125783×10⁻¹⁷). Thus, within numerical zero, the standard-frame coordinates are obtained from the input-frame coordinates by the approximate mapping (−x−z)/2, (x+y)/2, and (−y−z)/2, with no origin translation.

In the standard Fdd2 description, the asymmetric unit contains five independent crystallographic orbits. Rubidium occupies the eightfold site 8a with coordinate relation (0, 0, z), represented by (0, 0, 0.4839199999999999), so its single independent positional parameter is z = 0.4839199999999999. Phosphorus occupies a second, symmetry-distinct 8a orbit of the same coordinate form (0, 0, z), represented by (0, 0, 0.0011190000000000921), with independent parameter z = 0.0011190000000000921. These two 8a sublattices therefore both lie on the polar axis but at different heights along c.

The remaining atoms occupy general 16b positions. Hydrogen forms one 16b orbit with representative coordinates (0.044407000000000085, 0.323028, 0.3685039999999999), so x = 0.044407000000000085, y = 0.323028, and z = 0.3685039999999999. Oxygen is split into two inequivalent 16b sublattices. The first oxygen orbit is represented by (0.02540749999999998, 0.11169299999999995, 0.8699994999999999), with independent coordinates x = 0.02540749999999998, y = 0.11169299999999995, and z = 0.8699994999999999. The second oxygen orbit is represented by (0.11525349999999995, 0.4756465, 0.6122769999999997), with independent coordinates x = 0.11525349999999995, y = 0.4756465, and z = 0.6122769999999997. Multiplicities of 8, 8, 16, 16, and 16 for Rb, P, H, O, and O respectively account for the full face-centered conventional-cell content implied by the Fdd2 symmetry.

The input coordinates were rounded to six decimal places before correction. Three small precision corrections are part of the real input geometry and must be retained rather than idealized away. One oxygen atom at input fractional position (0.982899, 0.293715, 0.466286) is displaced by (0, 0, −9.999999999732445×10⁻⁷), i.e. a decrease of 10⁻⁶ in z only. A second oxygen atom at (0.783714, 0.9929, 0.267101) is displaced by (1.0000000000287557×10⁻⁶, 0, 0), i.e. an increase of 10⁻⁶ in x only. A third oxygen atom at (0.2571, 0.466286, 0.293715) is displaced by (0, −9.999999999732445×10⁻⁷, 0), i.e. a decrease of 10⁻⁶ in y only. These corrections preserve the actual input-cell geometry while leaving the stated standard-frame orbit description intact.
